name: Roberto De Zerbi

spellsCounted.reason: Three Serie A seasons (11th, 8th, 8th; record 62 points in 2020/21) with the highest possession share in Serie A in 2020/21; 2-3-5/2+3 build-up with press-baiting; Coaches' Voice, Left Back, TFA coverage. Start day approximate (sources say June/July 2018); end approximate (Shakhtar says he led it from 2021-05-25).

Super Cup win, top of the league when the war stopped the season (18 league games plus Champions League and Super Cup), most possession in Ukraine; Spielverlagerung-style build-up study (McCormack). Start date from Shakhtar statement quoted in search; end is the club announcement of the exit (Sky Italia reported termination on 2022-07-06).

6th in 2022/23 (first European place), Europa League group winners, the 'provocation' build-up that defined the profile; extensive tier A-B coverage. End: announced 2024-05-18, last match 2024-05-19 at Manchester United.

Ligue 1 runner-up 2024/25 and Champions League qualification; same 3-2-5/press-baiting model; left by mutual agreement 2026-02-11 after a 5-0 loss to PSG. Tactical coverage is thinner (one newsletter, one French match analysis); start date is the day The Athletic reported him confirmed.

Appointed to avoid relegation (done on the final day of 2025/26 with a 1-0 win over Everton, 7 games), then 2026/27 in progress (about 10 league games plus League Cup by 2026-11-06, so over 15 competitive matches). Move to a bigger job in some views; tactical coverage so far is mostly previews, not match analysis.

spellsExcluded.reason: Lower league start of career; no tactical coverage found.
Lega Pro; origin of the style per TFA/Ligue 1 (4-3-3/3-4-3 since Foggia) but no tier A-B study of that period found in this run; dates not verified.
Under 15 competitive matches (about 13) and seven consecutive defeats; sacked.
Relegated; praised for possession football but no dedicated tactical coverage found, and the sample is a struggling promoted side; exact end date not verified.

scopeNote: Excluded spells carry partial dates (Darfo Boario 2013-2014, Foggia 2014-2016, Benevento end 2018) because no day-level dates were verified. Covers Sassuolo (2018-06 to 2021-05), Shakhtar (2021-05 to 2022-07), Brighton (2022-09 to 2024-05), Marseille (2024-06 to 2026-02) and Tottenham (2026-03-31 to ongoing at 2026-11-06). The style is called press-baiting / provocation build-up (Sky, TFA) and positional play with a goalkeeper as third centre-back; the 'high line and aggressive counter-press' is partly right: sources (Coaches' Voice, Sky) say pressing is not the key aspect and he 'called pressing a gamble', while Premier League/Left Back describe man-oriented pressing. Sassuolo start day (2018-06-18) is not confirmed by a source read in this run (a search snippet said July 2018). Set pieces: the only evidence is his own disinterest. Marking: pressing is man-oriented in the first wave (Sassuolo 2019/20) and 'man-to-man' per the Premier League; no source states a marking scheme for Marseille or Tottenham.
openQuestions: Sassuolo start date: 2018-06-18 is unconfirmed; one search snippet said he arrived in July 2018.
Sassuolo end and Shakhtar start: Shakhtar says in charge since 2021-05-25; Sassuolo end set at 2021-05-24 by approximation.
Pressing: Sky quotes him calling pressing a gamble, while the Premier League and Left Back describe aggressive man-to-man pressing; both are kept as sources.
Marking at Marseille and Tottenham: no tier A-B source found on zonal vs man-oriented defending; opponents man-marking him is documented (Analytics FC) but not his own scheme.
Tottenham: 2025/26 relegation fight vs 2026/27 style are mixed in the sources; no match-level tactical analysis found. Wikipedia says a five-year contract, other reports say long-term.
Marseille: an Italian fantasy site says Rowe and Rabiot fought in the dressing room and were sold, and that he refused to lead training on 2025-03-30; tier D, unverified.
